name: Meal Penalty
tagline: Film payroll that pays your crew before they revolt.
positioning: Union-aware payroll built for the owner-operator running a lean production company, not a studio with a legal floor.

hero.h1: Payroll that survives a 14-hour shoot day.
hero.sub: Meal Penalty runs timecards, fringes, and union math for the two-person production company that can't afford a payroll department — or a lawsuit.

features.title: Golden time, calculated
features.description: We know when your grip crossed into double-time at 2am. Overtime, meal penalties, and turnaround are computed before the gaffer starts doing napkin math.

features.title: Union tables that update themselves
features.description: IATSE, DGA, SAG-AFTRA minimums baked in and refreshed when the contracts change, so you stop bookmarking PDFs you'll never read again.

features.title: Kit fees without the spreadsheet
features.description: Track equipment rentals, box fees, and reimbursements per person, per day, per project. It all lands in one clean deal memo.

features.title: Timecards from set, not email
features.description: Your AD approves hours from their phone between setups. No screenshots of a legal pad at wrap.

features.title: Year-end that isn't a horror film
features.description: W-2s, 1099s, and multi-state filings for the crew you flew in from three states away. We handle the paperwork you keep forgetting exists.

features.title: Deal memos that stick
features.description: Rates, roles, and terms locked per hire, so nobody 'remembers' a different day rate on payday.

testimonials.quote: I used to reconcile timecards at 1am in a hotel parking lot. Now the meal penalties calculate themselves and I actually sleep during a shoot. Genuinely rude how easy this is.
testimonials.name: Danielle Rourke

testimonials.quote: We're four people and a van. Meal Penalty is the only reason we can hire a union crew without a payroll company charging us like we're Warner Bros.
testimonials.name: Marcus Vellani

testimonials.quote: The union rate tables alone saved me from two grievances last quarter. It quietly knows more about my labor obligations than I do.
testimonials.name: Priya Anand

pricing.blurb: For the solo producer running one project at a time.
For working production companies juggling multiple crews.
For established shops with a real accountant and real exposure.

homepage.footerBlurb: Meal Penalty is film payroll for people who'd rather be on set. Not affiliated with any union, but fluent in all of them.
